summary: The narrator, after a horrifying ordeal, is reunited with Sarah and Steve in a flooded area. Steve explains he escaped Ramos, who had drugged him, and set a fire with ether to destroy the lab, and the group escapes downstream on the Usumacinta River. They are picked up, reach the Mayan ruin of Yaxchitan, and return by air to New York, with the narrator noting that readjusting to normal life, especially for Sarah, proves difficult.
one_line: Fictional narrative from Book 3 in which the narrator, Sarah and Steve escape by river after a lab fire and travel back to New York.
key_facts: Steve's bandaged nose was bleeding again when the narrator reunited with him.
Steve said Ramos came in to finish him off, but Steve was not as drugged out as Ramos thought.
Steve brought along Ramos's nine-millimeter silver automatic, which he carried in his belt.
Steve said he threw ether around and pitched a match to set the lab on fire.
The narrator suggested the group go with the current to reach the Usumacinta River.
The narrator reports that snakes and crocodiles were lurking in the roiling waters.
Sunrise broke through the last of the rain as the group rowed for midstream.
The group was picked up by a ragged vessel and dropped off at Yaxchitan.
Yaxchitan is described as a Mayan ruin on the western bank of the Usumacinta.
The group joined an American day-tour heading back to San Cristobal de las Casas.
From San Cristobal de las Casas they caught a prop flight to Cancun, then American Airlines to New York.
The narrator flew first-class without luggage and still has the MasterCard slip as proof.
Sarah experienced lapses of non-rationality and once tried to dive overboard.
The narrator says returning Sarah to normalcy, or the narrator to normalcy, was another struggle entirely.
